books.title: Kairos
books.author: Jenny Erpenbeck
books.synopsis: In late-1980s East Berlin, nineteen-year-old Katharina begins an affair with Hans, a married writer in his fifties. Their increasingly destructive relationship unfolds alongside the collapse of East Germany.
books.authorBio: Jenny Erpenbeck is a German novelist whose books include Visitation, The End of Days and Go, Went, Gone.
books.awards: International Booker Prize 2024 (with translator Michael Hofmann)

books.title: The Lake
books.author: Bianca Bellová
books.synopsis: Nami grows up beside a polluted, shrinking lake. Leaving his fishing village to search for his missing mother, he encounters a damaged world where survival demands courage and persistence.
books.authorBio: Bianca Bellová is a Czech writer, translator and interpreter with Bulgarian roots. The Lake received the European Union Prize for Literature.
books.awards: European Union Prize for Literature 2017; EBRD Literature Prize 2023 (with translator Alex Zucker)

books.title: My Stupid Intentions
books.author: Bernardo Zannoni
books.synopsis: Archy, a young stone marten, struggles to survive in a world of talking animals. Learning to read and write opens up questions about God, death and what it means to live with human awareness.
books.authorBio: Bernardo Zannoni is an Italian novelist. My Stupid Intentions is his debut novel, begun when he was twenty-one.

books.title: Dear Dickhead
books.author: Virginie Despentes
books.synopsis: An insulting social-media post starts an unlikely correspondence between novelist Oscar and actress Rebecca. Their exchanges confront addiction, ageing, celebrity and sexual misconduct while gradually making room for friendship.
books.authorBio: Virginie Despentes is a French novelist and filmmaker, known for King Kong Theory and the Vernon Subutex novels.

books.title: Glorious People
books.author: Sasha Salzmann
books.synopsis: Lena and Tatjana navigate the upheaval following the Soviet Union’s collapse. Their choices about migration, love and survival shape their daughters’ lives, linking the experiences of mothers and children across Ukraine and Germany.
books.authorBio: Sasha Salzmann is a writer whose Glorious People examines migration, identity and the effects of political upheaval across generations.
books.performerBio: Chan Yuen Yu Caroline is a performing artist whose work spans theatre, concerts, music videos and film. Her training includes acting, voice, physical performance and devised theatre.

books.title: Gerta
books.author: Kateřina Tučková
books.synopsis: After the liberation of Brno in 1945, Gerta Schnirch is expelled with other ethnic Germans despite having a Czech mother. Carrying her infant daughter, she begins a decades-long struggle with displacement, injustice and the possibility of forgiveness.
books.authorBio: Kateřina Tučková is a Czech novelist, playwright, art historian and curator. Her novels include Gerta and The Žítková Goddesses.
books.performerBio: Vincent Tang Ka-lai is a television presenter, master of ceremonies and educator. He read from Gerta at Commaa for the 2025 edition.

books.title: Sad Tiger
books.author: Neige Sinno
books.synopsis: Drawing on her experience of childhood sexual abuse, Sinno combines personal testimony with literary reflection. The book examines violence, memory and the limits of storytelling, asking how writing might help protect others.
books.authorBio: Neige Sinno is a French writer who has worked as a translator and literature professor. Her earlier books include Le Camion and La Vie des rats.
books.performerBio: Angela Yu is a Hong Kong poet who writes in Chinese, English and French. Her books include Juvie and Psycho in Paradise.

books.title: Perfection
books.author: Vincenzo Latronico
books.synopsis: Anna and Tom build an enviable life as creative professionals in Berlin. Behind the apartment, photographs and carefully managed appearances, their dissatisfaction exposes the gap between an ideal online image and everyday experience.
books.authorBio: Vincenzo Latronico is an Italian novelist, art critic and translator. Perfection is his fourth novel and his first translated into English.
books.performerBio: Elizabeth “Lilli” Chung is a writer, critic and CUHK researcher of Hong Kong literature. She co-organises Peel Street Poetry and OutLoudHK and co-founded Flow State.
books.awards: Shortlisted for the International Booker Prize 2025

books.title: The End
books.author: Attila Bartis
books.synopsis: After his mother’s death and his father’s release from prison, András Szabad moves to Budapest and discovers photography. His memories of family, artistic ambition and a consuming relationship form a portrait of life under authoritarianism.
books.authorBio: Attila Bartis is a Romanian-Hungarian writer whose fiction includes The End and Tranquility.
books.performerBio: Attila Gönczy is a Hungarian actor based in Hong Kong and the founder of VULGO Theatre and Aurelian Academy.

books.title: Fishing for the Little Pike
books.author: Juhani Karila
books.synopsis: Each summer Elina returns to Lapland with three days to catch a particular pike or face a fatal curse. This year supernatural creatures and a detective investigating a murder complicate her task.
books.authorBio: Juhani Karila is a Finnish author and journalist. His debut novel Fishing for the Little Pike followed two short-story collections and won several Finnish literary prizes.
books.awards: Kalevi Jäntti Prize; Tähtifantasia Prize; Jarkko Laine Prize
books.performerBio: Gavin Coates is a landscape architect, illustrator and author of environmental children’s books. He has taught landscape design and drawing at the University of Hong Kong.

books.title: Dubliners
books.author: James Joyce
books.synopsis: Fifteen stories follow ordinary Dublin lives through childhood, adolescence and adulthood. Moments of disappointment and revelation expose the distance between what people hope for and the lives they lead.
books.authorBio: James Joyce (1882–1941) was an Irish writer. Although he spent much of his adult life abroad, Dublin remained central to his fiction, including Ulysses and A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.
books.performerBio: Ki Kwok (郭梓祺) is a Hong Kong writer, educator and columnist whose work connects Chinese literature with Irish studies.

books.title: The City of Mist
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.synopsis: This collection returns to the mysterious atmosphere of the Cemetery of Forgotten Books novels. Its stories bring together unusual characters, hidden histories and the gothic imagination associated with Zafón’s Barcelona.
books.authorBio: Carlos Ruiz Zafón was a Spanish novelist best known for The Shadow of the Wind and the Cemetery of Forgotten Books series.
books.performerBio: Carlos Koo is an actor, also credited as Carlos Tin-Cheung Koo. His screen work includes Don’t Go Breaking My Heart.

books.title: First Blood
books.author: Amélie Nothomb
books.synopsis: Nothomb imagines her father’s life in his own voice, tracing the experiences and choices that formed him. The novel explores family, reconciliation and the personal history behind a life-threatening diplomatic crisis.
books.authorBio: Amélie Nothomb is a Belgian novelist. First Blood draws on the life of her father, the diplomat Patrick Nothomb.
books.performerBio: Rachel Smith is an artist, storyteller and educator based in Hong Kong. Her work includes paper and watercolour art, storytelling and the HK Mail Art Club.

books.title: Death at Intervals
books.author: José Saramago
books.synopsis: When people in an unnamed country stop dying, celebration gives way to practical and moral chaos. Death eventually resumes her work with advance warning letters, until one letter unexpectedly comes back.
books.authorBio: José Saramago (1922–2010) was a Portuguese novelist and the recipient of the 1998 Nobel Prize in Literature. His work has been translated into more than forty languages.

books.title: The Alaska Sanders Affair
books.author: Joël Dicker
books.synopsis: Eleven years after Alaska Sanders’s murder was apparently solved, writer Marcus Goldman and Sergeant Perry Gahalowood return to the case. New evidence unsettles the original verdict and reopens a complicated investigation.
books.authorBio: Joël Dicker is a Swiss novelist whose crime fiction includes The Truth About the Harry Quebert Affair and The Alaska Sanders Affair.

books.title: The Factory
books.author: Ihor Mysiak
books.synopsis: A group of men restores an abandoned factory near a forgotten village to manufacture machines promising happiness. Their enterprise becomes a satirical, reflective exploration of community, everyday pleasure and the need to protect life.
books.authorBio: Ihor Mysiak (1993–2023) was a Ukrainian poet and novelist. The Factory appeared in Ukrainian in 2022; he was killed while serving in Ukraine’s defence the following year.

books.title: Hey, Good Morning, How Are You?
books.author: Martina Hefter
books.synopsis:
Juno Isabella Flock is a dancer and performance artist who spends her days caring for her ailing husband, and her nights chatting to love scammers online. She’s aware of the risks these men pose – she’s watched a documentary about them – but she’s also discovered a heady freedom in these online conversations, and the things they allow her to say.

When Juno meets Owen_Wilson223 – or, to use his real name, Benu - she senses an immediate connection between them, even though they're separated by thousands of miles. Gradually, they reveal more and more about themselves to each other: about their real selves, and about who they really want to be. And just as Juno sees through Benu’s lies, he sees through hers too.

Hey, Good Morning, How Are You? is a whirlwind of a novel. It’s about yearning to stay young while age marches on; it’s about how to stay truthful while the internet changes everything; it’s about love and desire in all their many, conflicting forms. And most of all, it’s a novel about the way we are all connected, by the same constellations and the same night sky, however different our circumstances.
books.authorBio: Martina Hefter is an author and performer based in Leipzig. Her texts move between poetry, scenic forms of writing, and novelistic writing. She stages many of her texts in collaboration with other artists. In Germany, she has published three novels, and five volumes of poetry. Her novel Hey, Good Morning, How Are You? won the German Book Prize in 2024, and is her first work to be translated into English.

books.title: Ceilings
books.author: Zuzana Brabcová
books.synopsis: Awarded the Magnesia Litera Prose Book of the Year in 2013, CEILINGS is a polyphonic novel kin to the work of Leonora Carrington and Unica Zürn. Taking place in a mental hospital in Prague where the “narrator” is undergoing detox treatment for substance abuse, the borders blur between inner experience and the outer world, between reality and dream. As the walls and ceilings hemming in the desire for freedom fantastically break open as if into the unknown and gender fluidly shifts between brother and sister, who are one and the same, Brabcová’s flights of imagination portray how difficult it is to “come out of oneself” and to engage with the other in a multifarious world that demands it of us, no matter how ambivalently. Ceilings by Zuzana Brabcová is translated from the Czech by Tereza Veverka Novická and published by Twisted Spoon Press in 2025.
books.authorBio: The daughter of two literary historians, Brabcová (1959–2015) was born in Prague. Under the Communist regime, she was denied the right to attend university so she worked as a librarian, a hospital attendant and a cleaner. Following the Velvet Revolution, she worked as an editor. Her first novel Far from the Tree, initially published abroad in 1987, won the inaugural Jiří Orten Prize. Ceilings (2012), recently released in Tereza Veverka Novická’s powerful English translation, was her fourth novel, a vivid, hypnotic account of one woman’s transit through drug rehab. Her writing has been compared to Leonora Carrington and Unica Zürn, whose artwork appears on the cover.
books.awards: Magnesia Litera, Prose Book of the Year 2013

books.title: Poems New and Collected
books.author: Wisława Szymborska
books.synopsis: Poems spanning 1957–1997 explore ordinary life, history and human existence with wit, precision and philosophical curiosity.
books.authorBio: Wisława Szymborska (1923–2012) was a Polish poet, editor, translator and columnist. She received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1996.
books.nominationStatus: Book and Ztoryhome venue confirmed by organiser. Cover identifies the researched English edition.
